proof:
Grouping the convex combinations in the definition of $C$ gives $C_p=K_p$ by anchored compatibility. The closed tail of any linear observable on $S$ is left-continuous by continuity of measure from above on closed half-lines whose lower thresholds increase to the limit. For $0<q\le M$ its admissible thresholds thus form a nonempty closed initial interval with a finite right endpoint. This also applies to pure-base atomic tails and gives the intersection of closed linear quantile inequalities defining $\{b_{\rm base}\ge q\}$. If $u\ne0$, each fiber assigns zero mass to a single level of the observable by absolute continuity, so the tail is continuous and has value $q$ at the right endpoint. If two observables differ pointwise on $S$ by at most $\eta$, either tail at threshold $s$ is bounded by the other at $s-\eta$, giving the two quantile bounds. In particular this argument permits plateaus.

The threshold of each buffered cap is affine minus $\varepsilon f$, hence is convex on $C$. Applying the exact closed quantile criterion to every direction gives the asserted compact convex superlevel. For $\varepsilon=0$ the pure-base and nonvertical boundary-through-mark caps suffice because a halfspace containing a mark can be shifted inward to have the mark on its boundary. Thus $b_0$ has the asserted meaning.

For each nonvertical unit continuous normal, linear coarea on each fiber bounds the mass in the added strip of thickness $\varepsilon f(w)$ by $\varepsilon Lf(w)$, uniformly in the base tilt. The finite section bound follows by placing the fibers in a common ball. For $d=1$ each section has at most one point. The same inequalities hold for the infimum including the unchanged pure-base term. Compactness of all positive superlevels gives upper semicontinuity and attainment on $S$. At any interior sampled mark a centered ball in its own fiber gives a fixed positive lower bound for every through-mark cap, using a half-ball for a nonvertical direction and the full own fiber for a pure-base direction. Hence $Q_0>0$. The estimate yields the stated maximum bounds, and upper semicontinuity of $b_0$ puts each limiting maximizer in its $Q_0$-superlevel.

For $y\in\partial K_p$, choose a unit outward supporting normal and apply accepted fact 155691fc3768c06f with the anchored family at $p$. The opposite side of its lifted supporting inequality is a closed through-mark cap which contains at most a support slice in every fiber, so has zero mass. Thus $b_\varepsilon(p,y)=b_0(p,y)=0$. The compact set $\{w\in S:b_0(w)\ge Q_0/2\}$ stays a positive distance from each sampled own boundary, using the finiteness of $P$. For small $\varepsilon$ the uniform strip estimate puts all buffered maximizers in this set. The corresponding centered inballs bound both supporting gaps below, and the common shift is at most $\varepsilon\max_C f$, proving the uniform assertion.

For the energy examples, accepted fact 7227bbfcd12ad3d2 gives full-dimensional real fibers and their Hausdorff continuity, including boundary bases. For a sequence $(z_j,x_j)\to(z,x)$ in $C$ with $x\in\operatorname{int}C_z$, the centered fibers $C_{z_j}-x_j$ converge to $C_z-x$ in Hausdorff distance. If the latter contains a centered ball of radius $r>0$ and their distance is $\delta_j<r$, comparison of support functions sandwiches the former between $(1-\delta_j/r)(C_z-x)$ and $(1+\delta_j/r)(C_z-x)$. In particular $x_j$ is own-interior eventually. Inclusion monotonicity and affine covariance from d90ba05577427854 squeeze the energy between the corresponding factors $(1\pm\delta_j/r)^d$ times $E_{C_z}(x)$.

For an own-boundary limit, fix an inward unit support normal $e$ with $s=e\cdot x=\min_{C_z}e\cdot X$. For interior members of the sequence put $s_j=\min_{C_{z_j}}e\cdot X$ and $\delta_j=e\cdot x_j-s_j>0$. Both $s_j\to s$ and $\delta_j\to0$ by Hausdorff continuity. Test the energy with the admissible denominator $1+e\cdot(X-x_j)/(2\delta_j)$, which is at least $1/2$ on $C_{z_j}$. On a common bounded region its integrand with the fiber indicator is bounded by $2^{d+1}$. Below $e\cdot X=s$ the indicator is eventually zero, and above it the denominator tends to infinity. Dominated convergence gives the zero boundary limit. Finally the joint interior root concavity of 5aeb5916857f97a9 applies because each interpolated fiber contains the interpolated bodies and the marks combine interior balls. Approximation within each own fiber extends that concavity to $C$. The positive increasing concave power $d/(d+1)$ of the root gives the second buffer.
statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ and let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty and let each $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body. Assume $\sum_{p\in P}\lambda_p K_p\subseteq K_z$ for every convex combination with $\sum_p\lambda_p p=z\in P$. Put $B=\operatorname{conv}P$, $S=\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$, $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and let $\mu=\sum_{p\in P}\delta_p\otimes(\mathbf1_{K_p}\,dx)$ have total mass $M$. Write $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$. Work relative to $\operatorname{aff}B$ in the base. Let $f:C\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous and concave, positive on each own-fiber interior and zero on each own-fiber boundary.

For $\varepsilon\ge0$ define $b_\varepsilon(z,x)$ as the minimum of the closed pure-base depth $b_{\rm base}(z)$ for the atomic masses $|K_p|$ and the infimum over all base vectors $a$ and unit $u\in\mathbb R^d$ of $\mu\{a\cdot Z+u\cdot X\ge a\cdot z+u\cdot x-\varepsilon f(z,x)\}$. In base rank zero put $b_{\rm base}=M$. In particular $b_0$ is the original closed mixed depth. For $0<q\le M$ set $c_q(a,u)=\sup\{c:\mu\{a\cdot Z+u\cdot X\ge c\}\ge q\}$. Then the exact buffered region is the compact convex set
$$
D_{q,\varepsilon}
=\{(z,x)\in C:b_{\rm base}(z)\ge q,\
 a\cdot z+u\cdot x-\varepsilon f(z,x)\le c_q(a,u)\ \text{for every }a,\ \|u\|=1\}.
$$
For fixed $q$, the quantile changes by at most $\sup_S|(a-a')\cdot Z+(u-u')\cdot X|$ under replacement of $(a,u)$ by $(a',u')$.

With $L=\sum_{p\in P}\sup_{\|u\|=1,s\in\mathbb R}\mathcal H^{d-1}(K_p\cap\{u\cdot X=s\})$, one has $0\le b_\varepsilon(w)-b_0(w)\le\varepsilon Lf(w)$ throughout $C$. The maxima $Q_\varepsilon=\max_S b_\varepsilon$ are attained and $0<Q_0\le Q_\varepsilon\le Q_0+\varepsilon L\max_C f$. Every cluster point of maximizing marks as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ attains $Q_0$. For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, all maximizing $(p,y)$ stay a uniformly positive distance from $\partial K_p$ and all shifted own thresholds $u\cdot y-\varepsilon f(p,y)$ stay uniformly between the two support levels.

Admissible buffers include $E_{C_z}(x)^{1/d}$ and $E_{C_z}(x)^{1/(d+1)}$, each extended by zero at own-fiber boundary marks, with $E$ the projective energy of fact d90ba05577427854.
title: Closed quantile regions for concavely buffered mixed depth
